title: Rice Pilaf Mix
intro: Plain rice is easy enough, but a good pilaf needs the right balance of herbs and seasoning. This mix has everything measured together, so the rice is ready to go whenever you want a simple, savory side dish.

fields.serving_size: about ⅓ cup dry mix, used to make one serving of rice pilaf.
whats_in_jar: 1 tablespoon dried onion in minced form
what_to_add: Butter/olive oil for cooking, as preferred
instructions: Add the rice, dried onion, garlic powder, parsley, oregano, paprika, salt, and black pepper to a large bowl.
Stir well so the seasonings are evenly mixed with and throughout the rice.
Add this seasoning mixture to a clean, dry 1-quart jar or airtight container.
Seal the lid tightly and label the jar with the name and date.
For one serving, measure out about ⅓ cup of the dry mix. Then, cook with the liquid and a small amount of butter or oil.
fields.storage: Place the dry mix in an airtight jar in the pantry for up to 6 months. Keep away from steam and moisture.

title: Beans and Rice Mix
intro: This is a good one to have around when the pantry looks a little bare. The rice and seasoning are ready in the jar; add a can of beans when you're ready to cook, and dinner is already half done.

fields.serving_size: about ⅓ cup dry mix, used for one serving of beans and rice.
instructions: Add the rice, dried onion, chili powder, garlic powder, cumin powder, paprika, oregano, salt, and black pepper in a large bowl. Combine them all.
Mix them all thoroughly so the seasonings are evenly mixed in the rice.
Shift into a clean, completely dry airtight container.
Seal the jar. Label it.
fields.storage: Place the jar properly sealed in a cool, dry pantry. Store it for up to 6 months.

title: Instant Mashed Potato Mix
intro: There are days when peeling and boiling potatoes just isn't worth the extra work. This jar keeps instant potato flakes and the seasonings together, giving you a well-seasoned starting point for creamy mashed potatoes in just a few minutes.

fields.serving_size: about ½ cup dry potato mix, used for one serving of mashed potatoes.
instructions: Put the potato flakes, dried onion, garlic powder, parsley, salt, black pepper, and paprika in a large bowl.
Whisk gently until the seasoning is evenly distributed without crushing the potato flakes.
Transfer the mixture to an airtight container large enough to hold it loosely.
Seal and label.
When you want to cook, prepare the meal by using this pre-mix seasoning with hot milk and water, then stir in butter to taste.
fields.storage: Keep sealed in a dry pantry for up to 6 months. Store away from steam and moisture, as they can make the potato flakes clump.

title: Sloppy Joe Seasoning Mix
intro: Sloppy Joe night gets much easier when the seasoning is already mixed and waiting in the pantry. The seasoning is already balanced in the jar, so there’s no opening the spice cabinet and trying to remember what went into the last batch.

fields.serving_size: about ½ tablespoon dry seasoning, for about ¼ pound of ground beef.
whats_in_jar: 2 teaspoons dry mustard in powder form
instructions: Add all the dry seasonings to a small bowl, and whisk and mix them.
By whisking, any clumps of chili powder or onion will be broken up, making a smooth blend.
Pour the blend into a small airtight jar or spice container.
Seal tightly and label.
fields.storage: Keep the seasoning jar in your spice cabinet and use within 6 months for the best flavor. Keep the lid properly closed between uses.

title: Quinoa Pilaf Mix
intro: Quinoa is easy to keep on hand, but I don't always want it plain. This jar takes care of that part ahead of time, with the quinoa and seasonings already together so a simple side is ready whenever you need one.

fields.serving_size: about ⅓ cup dry mix, used to make one serving of quinoa pilaf.
whats_in_jar: 2 cups of uncooked quinoa, rinsed & dried
instructions: Rinse the quinoa thoroughly under cold water and spread it on a clean towel or tray until completely dry.
Combine the dry quinoa with the dried onion, garlic powder, parsley, thyme, paprika, salt, and black pepper.
Stir well so the seasonings are thoroughly mixed in one another.
Shift the seasoning to a clean, airtight jar or container. Add a label on it.
fields.storage: Once the quinoa is completely dry, keep the mix sealed in the pantry for up to 6 months.

title: Stuffing Mix
intro: I like having stuffing ready before the holidays are anywhere in sight. This jar keeps the bread cubes and seasonings together, so when you want a pan of stuffing, you only need to add the butter and broth and get it into the oven.

fields.serving_size: about ¾ cup dry stuffing mix, used for one serving of prepared stuffing.
instructions: Put the dried bread cubes in a large bowl.
Add and sprinkle the dried onion, parsley, sage, thyme, rosemary, salt, and pepper over the bread.
Toss gently until the seasonings are evenly distributed.
Shift the mixture to a large airtight container or divide it between smaller jars.
Close the jar and label it according to the prep date.
fields.storage: Keep completely dry and tightly sealed in the pantry for up to 3 months.

title: Mac and Cheese Mix
intro: This is the kind of jar that earns its space because everyone knows what dinner is when you pull it out. The pasta and cheese sauce ingredients are already portioned together, so you don't have to hunt through the pantry for a box or measure out a homemade sauce.

fields.serving_size: about 4 ounces of dry pasta and sauce mix, for one serving.
instructions: Combine the powdered cheddar, milk powder, cornstarch, mustard powder, garlic powder, onion powder, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
Mix thoroughly so the cornstarch and seasonings are evenly distributed.
Add the dry macaroni and toss until everything is well combined.
Transfer to a large airtight container or divide into six portions, and label it.
Keep the container sealed, and when you want to use it, 2 ounces of the dry mix will go for one serving.
Also, add milk and butter when preparing.
fields.storage: Keep sealed in a cool, dry cupboard. For the best quality, use within 3 months or follow the shortest date on the packaged cheese powder.

title: Loaded Baked Potato Topping Mix
intro: A baked potato can be an easy, filling dinner when the toppings are ready to go. Keep this pre-mix in the pantry for those times when you want something warm and filling. That too, without chopping a long list of toppings or having to cook bacon from scratch.

fields.serving_size: about 2 tablespoons dry topping mix, for one baked potato.
whats_in_jar: ½ cup shelf-stable real bacon bits
instructions: Combine the bacon bits, powdered cheddar, dried chives, garlic powder, onion powder, smoked paprika, black pepper, and salt in a bowl.
Stir until well-mixed, and transfer to a properly cleaned, dry, airtight container.
Label the jar according to the date prepared and by writing the name of seasoning mix.
Use about 2 tablespoons of the topping mix on each baked potato. Add sour cream just before serving.
fields.storage: Use shelf-stable bacon bits and keep the finished mix tightly sealed in the pantry for up to 3 months.

title: Fried Rice Seasoning Mix
intro: Leftover rice has a way of sitting in the refrigerator until nobody knows what to do with it. Keep this seasoning in the pantry, and that container of rice can turn into a quick skillet dinner with an egg, some vegetables, and whatever cooked protein you have on hand.

fields.serving_size: about 2 teaspoons of dry seasoning for one serving of fried rice.
whats_in_jar: 2 tablespoons of soy sauce powder, preferably low-sodium one
instructions: Add all ingredients to a small bowl.
Stir thoroughly, making sure the soy sauce powder and sugar are evenly distributed.
Transfer the seasoning to a small airtight jar, then seal and label it.
fields.storage: Store the seasoning in a small airtight jar away from heat and direct sunlight. It will keep well for about 6 months.

title: Couscous Seasoning Mix
intro: Couscous cooks quickly, which is exactly why I like having the seasoning measured ahead of time too. When you need a side in a hurry, the jar and a little hot water are most of the work.

fields.serving_size: about ⅓ cup dry couscous mix, for one serving.
instructions: Add the couscous, dried onion, garlic powder, parsley, oregano, paprika, salt, and black pepper to a bowl.
Stir until the seasonings are evenly mixed through the couscous.
Transfer the seasoning mixture to a clean, dry, airtight jar or container.
Seal and label.
Measure about ⅓ cup of the dry mix for one serving. Prepare with hot water and finish with butter or olive oil.
fields.storage: Store tightly sealed in a dry pantry for up to 6 months. A dry storage spot helps keep the couscous loose and easy to measure.

title: Cheesy Scalloped Potato Mix
intro: Scalloped potatoes are worth making, but measuring out a cheese sauce from scratch isn't always ideal on a weeknight. This jar keeps the dry sauce ingredients together, so you can add the potatoes and milk when you're ready.

fields.serving_size: about 2 tablespoons dry sauce mix, for about ¼ pound of sliced potatoes.
instructions: Combine the powdered cheddar, milk powder, cornstarch, dried onion, garlic powder, salt, pepper, and paprika.
Whisk well to break up any lumps.
Transfer the dry sauce mix to an airtight jar.
Seal and label.
Use about 2 tablespoons of the dry mix for each ¼ pound of sliced potatoes. Add milk and butter when preparing.
fields.storage: Place the jar tightly sealed in a cool, dry pantry. Store it for up to 6 months.

title: Hearty Lentil and Rice Mix
intro: This is a good pantry jar for the days when you want something filling without needing meat. The lentils, rice, and seasonings are already together, so you can make a warm one-pot meal with ingredients that are easy to keep on hand.

fields.serving_size: about ¼ cup dry lentil-and-rice mix, for one serving of the finished dish.
whats_in_jar: 1 cup brown lentils, dried after cleaning
instructions: Check the lentils and remove any debris or stones.
Combine the lentils, rice, dried onion, garlic powder, cumin, paprika, oregano, salt, pepper, and turmeric.
Stir thoroughly so the seasonings are evenly distributed through the grains and lentils.
Transfer to a clean, dry airtight container.
Seal and label.
Use about ¼ cup dry mix per serving. Add water or broth and cook until both the rice and lentils are tender.
fields.storage: Keep sealed in the pantry for up to 6 months. Check that the mix is completely dry before each use.

title: Hamburger Helper–Style Beef and Mac Mix
intro: Some nights call for a dinner that gets one pan dirty and feeds everybody. Keep this mix ready for those evenings; brown some ground beef, add the jar, and you've already got most of the meal accounted for.

fields.serving_size: about 2 ounces dry pasta and seasoning mix, for one serving.
instructions: Combine the dried onion, paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, mustard powder, salt, pepper, and parsley.
Add the elbow macaroni and toss until evenly coated with the seasoning mixture.
Transfer everything to a clean, dry, airtight container, and seal it properly.
Label the jar to use for later.
fields.storage: Store the pasta mix in a tightly sealed jar. Place the jar in a cool, dry cupboard for up to 3 months.

title: Herb and Butter Rice Mix
intro: Plain rice is useful, but sometimes dinner needs a little more going on. This jar keeps the herbs and seasonings with the rice, so adding butter later is enough to turn it into a side that doesn't taste like an afterthought.

fields.serving_size: about ⅓ cup dry mix, for one serving of herb rice.
instructions: Add all the seasonings in a large bowl.
Mix them all until the seasonings are properly mixed and distributed with each other.
Transfer the seasoning mix to an airtight jar and seal it properly.
Label it with its name and date, and use about ⅓ cup dry mix per serving and cook with water or broth. Finish with butter.
fields.storage: Store tightly sealed in the pantry for up to 6 months. Store away from steam and direct heat to preserve the dried herbs.

title: Garlic Parmesan Pasta Base Mix
intro: This is one of those pantry helpers I like to have on hand for nights when the original dinner plan disappears. The pasta and dry sauce ingredients are already measured together, so butter and milk are all you need to turn the jar into a creamy pasta dish.

fields.serving_size: about 2 ounces dry pasta and sauce mix, for one serving.
whats_in_jar: 12 ounces of pasta; mostly use penne or rotini for this mix
instructions: Add the powdered Parmesan, milk powder, cornstarch, garlic powder, parsley, pepper, and salt.
Mix thoroughly until the powders are evenly distributed.
Add the pasta. Mix well.
Transfer to an airtight container large enough to hold the mixture without crushing the pasta.
Seal and label.
Use 2 ounces of the dry mix per serving. Add milk and butter when preparing.
fields.storage: Keep the mix sealed in the jar. Store the jar in a cool, dry pantry for up to 3 months.

title: Taco and Burrito Bowl Seasoning Kit
intro: This jar is made for the nights when everyone wants to build their own bowl. The rice and seasoning are ready together, and once you add cooked meat or beans and whatever toppings are in the fridge, dinner can go straight to the table.

fields.serving_size: about ⅓ cup dry rice and seasoning mix, for one bowl.
what_to_add: Cooked chicken, beef, or ground turkey
instructions: Combine the instant rice and all seasonings in a large bowl.
Mix thoroughly so the spices are properly mixed through the rice.
Transfer the mix to a clean, dry, airtight container and label it.
fields.storage: Keep tightly sealed in the pantry for up to 6 months. Slightly shake before using if the seasonings have settled.

title: One-Pot Chicken and Rice Mix
intro: There is something nice about having the rice and seasoning already measured when you're making a one-pot dinner. Add the chicken and the other fresh ingredients when you're ready, and you can get everything cooking without stopping to figure out the spice mixture first.

fields.serving_size: about ⅓ cup dry rice and seasoning mix, for one serving.
whats_in_jar: 1 tablespoon of onion, in minced form after drying
instructions: Add the rice, dried onion, and seasonings to a bowl, and mix them together.
Transfer to a clean, dry 1-quart jar or airtight container, then seal the container.
Label the jar according to the name of seasoning.
fields.storage: Place the seasoning mix in a cool, dry pantry for up to 6 months.

title: Sheet-Pan Dinner Seasoning and Starch Mix
intro: Sheet-pan dinners are supposed to be easy, and this jar helps keep them that way. The dry seasoning and starch are ready to toss with your protein and vegetables, so you can prep the whole pan without pulling out a handful of spice containers.

fields.serving_size: about ⅓ cup dry mix, for one portion of the sheet-pan dinner.
instructions: Combine the instant rice, dried onion, garlic powder, paprika, oregano, thyme, salt, and pepper.
Stir all these things well so the seasonings are properly mixed with the rice.
Pour the mixture into an airtight container. Seal the container with a lid properly so no air enters.
Label it and use about ⅓ cup dry mix per portion. Add the protein, vegetables, and oil when preparing.
fields.storage: Keep the jar tightly sealed in the pantry, and you can easily use it for up to 6 months.

title: Chicken Fajita Rice Bowl Mix
intro: This one is for those nights when chicken, peppers, and rice are already on the grocery list. Having the rice and fajita seasoning together means you can cook the components without making a separate seasoning blend while everything else is going.

fields.serving_size: about ⅓ cup dry rice and seasoning mix, for one rice bowl.
instructions: Take a bowl and add all the ingredients, such as the instant rice, chili powder, paprika, cumin, garlic and onion powder, oregano, salt, and pepper, to it.
Mix all these things until the seasoning is evenly distributed with the rice thoroughly.
Transfer the prepared pre-mix to a clean container and seal it tightly to keep it airtight.
Then, label the jar for future ease with the name and date.
When you want to prepare, use about ⅓ cup dry mix per bowl. Add cooked chicken, sliced peppers, and water when preparing.
fields.storage: Store the mix jar tightly sealed in a cool, dry pantry. Keep it stored for up to 6 months. Keep the jar away from the stove so the spices aren't exposed to heat and steam.

title: Cheesy Taco Rice Skillet Mix
intro: Who doesn’t like a skillet dinner without a pile of meal preparation? This pre-mix helps you because the rice, taco seasoning, and cheese sauce ingredients are already together. So, with cooked ground beef and a few fresh additions, the jar will turn into a yummy skillet dinner.

fields.serving_size: about ⅓ cup dry rice and cheese mix, for one serving.
whats_in_jar: ½ cup of cheddar cheese, powdered
instructions: In a bowl, add the instant rice, powdered cheddar, chili powder, cumin, garlic powder, onion powder, paprika, salt, and pepper.
Mix and stir all of these thoroughly so the cheese powder and seasonings are evenly mixed with each other.
Then add this mix to an airtight container and label it.
Add cooked ground beef and water when preparing.
fields.storage: You can store this seasoning premix by tightly sealing the jar and keeping it in a cool, dry pantry for up to 3 months.

title: Southwest Quinoa Bowl Mix
intro: Quinoa can be a little plain on its own, especially when you're trying to make a quick lunch. This jar handles the seasoning ahead of time, so once the quinoa is cooked, you can add your protein and toppings and call it a meal.

fields.serving_size: about ⅓ cup dry quinoa and seasoning mix, for one bowl.
what_to_add: Cooked chicken, beef, or ground turkey
instructions: Rinse the quinoa thoroughly and let it dry completely before mixing.
Once dried, mix the quinoa with all seasonings like chili powder, cumin, paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, oregano, salt, and pepper.
Mix everything by stirring well, then place it in a clean, dry, airtight container.
fields.storage: Once the quinoa is completely dry, keep the mix sealed in the pantry for up to 6 months.

title: Slow Cooker Pot Roast Seasoning Mix
intro: This jar helps you get through a busy week without hassle. The seasoning is perfectly measured. So, just add the roast and veggies to the slow cooker without building a spice mixture.

fields.serving_size: about 1 tablespoon dry seasoning, for about 6 ounces of pot roast and vegetables.
instructions: Add onion powder, garlic powder, paprika, parsley, thyme, rosemary, salt, pepper, and cornstarch to a bowl.
Whisk thoroughly to distribute the cornstarch and break up any clumps.
Transfer the blend to a small airtight jar and label it.
Use the full seasoning mix for one slow-cooker pot roast, or measure about 1 tablespoon for each portion when scaling the recipe.
fields.storage: To store it, keep the jar tightly sealed in a cool, dry pantry. It's best used within 6 months while the herbs and spices are still at their most fragrant.

title: Slow Cooker Chicken and Gravy Mix
intro: A slow cooker dinner feels even easier when the gravy base is already in the pantry. This mix gives you the seasoned gravy portion ahead of time, so when you're ready to make chicken, you can get the cooker going instead of measuring flour, herbs, and seasonings at the last minute.

fields.serving_size: about 2 tablespoons dry gravy and seasoning mix, for one serving of chicken and gravy.
instructions: Add all the ingredients to a small bowl.
Whisk until the powders are evenly distributed.
Transfer to an airtight jar, seal, and label.
Label clearly as Chicken and Gravy Mix.
Use the full jar for one slow-cooker batch, or about 2 tablespoons for one serving when scaling the recipe.
fields.storage: Keep the jar properly sealed in a cool, dry pantry. Store it for up to 6 months. Shake the jar before measuring.

title: Slow Cooker Beef Chili Mix
intro: Chili is one of those meals I like having a backup plan for. Keep this jar beside the canned beans and tomatoes, and when you have ground beef or stew meat ready to use, the seasoning is already handled.

fields.serving_size: about 1½ tablespoons dry chili seasoning, for one serving (1 pound beef) of prepared chili.
whats_in_jar: 2 teaspoons dried onion, in minced form
instructions: Put the chili powder, paprika, cumin, garlic powder, onion powder, oregano, salt, black pepper, and cayenne in a small bowl.
Whisk well to evenly mix the spices.
Transfer the blend to a small airtight jar.
Seal and label.
Use the full jar to season one batch of slow-cooker chili. If scaling the recipe, use about 1½ tablespoons per serving.
fields.storage: Store the jar tightly sealed in a cool, dry pantry for approx. 6 months.

title: Shepherd's Pie Mix
intro: Shepherd's pie has a few separate parts, so having one of them ready ahead of time makes a difference. This jar takes care of the seasoning and potato topping, leaving you to cook the meat and vegetables when you're ready to put the whole thing together.

fields.serving_size: about 1 ½ tbsp seasoning along with ¾ cup dry potato topping plus seasoning, for one serving of shepherd's pie.
whats_in_jar: ½ teaspoon black pepper, freshly and properly ground
½ teaspoon paprika in powder form
instructions: Add the seasoning ingredients in a bowl.
In a separate bowl, combine the potato flakes, garlic powder, salt, and black pepper.
Mix the two components with each other throughout. Or, layer them separately in the jar if you want the potato topping to stay distinct.
Transfer to a large airtight container and seal.
Label it clearly, and you’re set for later use.
fields.storage: Keep the dry mix sealed in a cool, dry pantry and keep it stored for up to 6 months. Keep the potato flakes dry to prevent moisture.

title: Taco Seasoning
intro: The taco seasoning I personally used to make one dinner at a time now lives in a jar. 2 tablespoons is enough for a pound of ground meat, so for the next taco night you don't have to remember the complete spice lineup.

fields.serving_size: about 2 tablespoons dry seasoning, enough for 1 pound of meat
instructions: Put the chili powder, paprika, cumin, garlic powder, onion powder, oregano, salt, black pepper, and cayenne into a bowl.
Then, pick up a fork and use it in the bowl to break apart any little clumps of garlic powder or chili powder.
Then mix all the powdery seasonings for about 30 seconds, making sure the salt and cayenne aren't sitting in one spot.
Once everything is properly mixed into each other, forming a new powder blend, spoon the finished product into an airtight jar.
Label the jar and close its lid firmly.
fields.storage: Place the jar in a cool, dry place or your dry kitchen pantry. Protect it from heat and direct light. My recommendation is to use within 6 months to get the freshest flavor.

title: Italian Seasoning
intro: This is one of those jars that quietly gets used all week. Pasta sauce, roasted vegetables, chicken, soup, garlic bread, or when a recipe needs a handful of dried herbs, this is usually the one I grab.

fields.serving_size: about 1 tablespoon dry blend for one serving
ingredients: 1 teaspoon properly crushed red pepper flakes
what_to_add: 1–2 teaspoons seasoning per pound of meat or vegetables
Or 1 tablespoon per 24 ounces of pasta sauce
instructions: Pour the basil, oregano, parsley, thyme, rosemary, marjoram, and red pepper flakes into a bowl.
Break the large rosemary pieces by rubbing them in between your fingers. Smaller pieces go best in seasoning blends.
Then, mix everything together with a spoon for proper mingling with one another.
Fill a clean spice jar and tap the bottom lightly on the counter to settle the herbs before putting on the lid.
fields.storage: Store airtight in a dark, dry cabinet. The blend keeps well for about 6 months.

title: Poultry Seasoning
intro: Chicken loves to show up on the dinner table again and again. With the seasoning already mixed, you can just grab the chicken, an airtight jar, and get on with the rest of dinner in minutes.

fields.serving_size: about 1 tsp dry seasoning per pound of chicken
ingredients: 1 tablespoon onion powder, in dried form
what_to_add: 1 teaspoon seasoning per pound of chicken or turkey
1 tablespoon olive oil or melted butter, if desired
instructions: Add the measured sage, thyme, rosemary, parsley, marjoram, onion powder, garlic powder, and pepper to a bowl.
Crush any large rosemary pieces by rubbing them between your fingers. This way, they will get closer in size to the other herbs.
Stir well until the powders evenly coat and get mixed thoroughly with the dried herbs.
Pour into a clean, dry jar and close tightly.
fields.storage: Keep this container of pre-mix blend tightly sealed in the pantry. Also, keep it away from steam and sunlight. Use within about 6 months for the best flavor.

title: All-Purpose Seasoning Salt
intro: This salt seasoning adds a different flavor than regular salt. It's useful on potatoes and eggs, but I usually use it just as often on vegetables, chicken, or burgers when I need a little extra flavor.

fields.serving_size: about 1 teaspoon dry seasoning will suffice one serving
ingredients: ¼ cup of fine sea salt
what_to_add: Or ½ teaspoon per pound of vegetables or potatoes
instructions: Add the salt to a bowl first, then sprinkle the paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, parsley, pepper, oregano, and mustard over it.
Mix for 30 to 45 seconds, scraping around the bottom of the bowl. This is to ensure that the heavier salt doesn't lie at the bottom without mixing with other seasonings.
Shift the finished seasoning blend into a dry spice jar.
Close the lid and shake the jar firmly for several seconds to finish distributing the mixture.
Label it and store for use in the future for a quick and easy meal.
fields.storage: Store in a dry spice cabinet with the lid tightly closed. It will keep well for about a year as long as no moisture gets into the jar.

title: Garlic Herb Blend
intro: Butter, garlic and dried herbs are potential enough to resolve a lot of dinner hurdles. This garlic herb blend keeps that combination ready for rice, vegetables, chicken, potatoes, or a piece of toast that needs something extra.

fields.serving_size: about 1 tablespoon dry blend
ingredients: 2 tablespoons of garlic, in powder form
what_to_add: 1 teaspoon per pound of meat or vegetables
Or 1 tablespoon mixed into 4 tablespoons softened butter
instructions: Add the parsley, basil, thyme, oregano, and rosemary to a bowl.
Add the garlic powder, pepper, and salt.
Stir with a spoon until the garlic powder and salt are no longer concentrated in one area.
If the rosemary pieces are large, pinch them into smaller pieces as you mix.
Pour into an airtight jar and close securely.
fields.storage: Keep it stored and sealed in a cool, dry pantry. For the strongest garlic and herb flavor, use within 6 months.

title: Lemon Pepper Seasoning
intro: I use this seasoning more often on fish and seafood, but it isn't limited to seafood. A little over roasted potatoes or chicken gives dinner that lemon-and-pepper flavor without having to zest a lemon at the last minute.

fields.serving_size: about 1 teaspoon dry seasoning will be used for one person's meal.
ingredients: 3 tablespoons of lemon peel in dried form
what_to_add: 1 teaspoon per pound of chicken or fish
½ teaspoon per pound of vegetables or potatoes
instructions: Check the dried lemon peel for any unusually large pieces and break them into smaller bits with your fingers.
Add the lemon peel and black pepper to a bowl.
Then, add garlic powder, onion powder, parsley, and salt to the same bowl.
Mix all of them together until the lemon peel is spread evenly throughout the pepper and powders.
Transfer to a dry spice jar and seal properly after labelling the container.
fields.storage: Keep the jar tightly closed in a cool, dry cabinet. It is best used within 6 months, and make sure to use a dry spoon when measuring.

title: Cajun Seasoning
intro: Sometimes you crave for not a salty seasoning, but a seasoning that has a perfect smoky heat flavor. This Cajun Seasoning is an ideal blend for chicken, shrimp, sausage, or vegetables when you want seasoning with a little heat.

fields.serving_size: about 1 tablespoon premix for a single meal
ingredients: 3 tablespoons of paprika in powdered form
2 teaspoons of finely ground black pepper
what_to_add: 1 tablespoon per pound of meat or seafood
2 teaspoons per pound of vegetables or potatoes
instructions: Measure the paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, oregano, thyme, black pepper, salt, and cayenne into a bowl.
Stir slowly at first so the cayenne and paprika don't puff out of the bowl.
Once the spices are mixed, give them another few stirs from the bottom upward.
Funnel the blend into a clean jar, or spoon it in carefully.
Seal and label.
fields.storage: Store in a tightly closed jar away from heat and moisture. It keeps well in the pantry for about 6 months.

title: BBQ Dry Rub
intro: Having this super-quick BBQ dry seasoning mix in your cabinet means you can season meat in no time, and the jar goes straight back into the cabinet for many next times.

fields.serving_size: approx. 2 tablespoons of this dry rub will be enough for about 1 pound of meat
what_to_add: 1 tablespoon dry rub per pound of pork, chicken, or beef
1 tablespoon olive oil, if desired, to help the rub adhere
instructions: Put the brown sugar in a bowl and press out any hard lumps with the back of a spoon.
Add the paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, chili powder, black pepper, salt, mustard, and cayenne.
Work the mixture between your fingers to break up any remaining brown sugar pieces.
Once the rub looks evenly colored, transfer it to a completely dry jar.
Seal immediately so no air can enter the jar.
fields.storage: Place the jar tightly sealed in a cool, dry pantry. Because of the brown sugar, use within about 3 months for the best texture.

title: Fajita Seasoning
intro: Peppers and onions are easy. The part I don't want to measure every time is the seasoning. This jar handles that job, whether the skillet is getting chicken, steak, shrimp, or vegetables.

fields.serving_size: about 2 tablespoons dry seasoning, enough for 1 pound of meat or vegetables
instructions: Start with the chili powder, paprika, and cumin in a bowl.
Add the garlic and onion powder, oregano, salt, and pepper to the bowl.
Stir with a whisk until the color looks even throughout.
Pour into a spice jar, using a small funnel if you have one. Label it too.
Close the jar tightly and give it a few shakes before putting it away.
fields.storage: Store sealed in a cool, dry cabinet away from direct heat. Use within about 6 months to enjoy best flavor.

title: Chili Powder Blend
intro: It is not necessary to have 10 different spice jars arranged on the counter every time you crave for a pot of chili. Whenever you want to prepare a pot, this deeper, well-balanced blend provides you with a constant starting point and the optimum flavor.

fields.serving_size: about 2 tablespoons dry blend is best for one serving of chili pot
instructions: Add the paprika and cumin to a bowl and mix them with each other to combine them properly.
Then, add the garlic powder, onion powder, oregano, black pepper, cayenne, and salt to the mixture of paprika and cumin
Run a fork through all these seasonings several times to break up any powdery clumps.
Transfer to an airtight jar. Tap the jar on the counter, just a gentle tap, to settle the blend.
Close tightly and label it.
fields.storage: Keep in a tightly sealed spice jar in a cool, dry pantry. The blend is best used within 6 months.

title: Everything Bagel Seasoning
intro: You'll start looking for reasons to use this once it's in the cabinet. Sprinkle it on anything that needs a little crunch and savory flavor, including potatoes, avocado, eggs, and toast.

fields.serving_size: about 1 tablespoon dry seasoning
ingredients: 2 tablespoons of minced garlic in dried form
what_to_add: 1 teaspoon per bagel or slice of toast
instructions: Put the sesame seeds and poppy seeds into a small bowl.
Add the dried garlic, dried onion, and salt.
Stir gently rather than whisking so the seeds stay intact.
Spoon the mixture into a small airtight jar.
Give the jar a slight shake whenever the ingredients settle between uses.
fields.storage: Place the jar tightly sealed in a cool, dry pantry. As it contains sesame and poppy seeds, use within about 3 months for the freshest flavor.

title: Blackening Seasoning
intro: When I want a browned, well-seasoned exterior without creating a spice blend at the last minute, I enjoy this one. This blend is perfect for fish and chicken, but it works well on veggies too.

fields.serving_size: about 1 tablespoon dry seasoning
what_to_add: 1 tablespoon seasoning per pound of chicken, fish, shrimp, or vegetables
1 tablespoon olive oil or melted butter for coating, if desired
instructions: Measure the paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, thyme, oregano, black pepper, salt, and cayenne into a bowl.
Stir with a fork until the herbs are broken apart and the powders are evenly mixed.
Pour the blend into an airtight jar.
Wipe the jar rim if any seasoning has collected there, then close the lid firmly.
fields.storage: Store in a dry spice cabinet away from heat and sunlight. Use within 6 months for the best flavor.

title: Pumpkin Pie Spice Blend
intro: Every time pumpkin season arrives, there's no need to measure five different spices. From pie to muffins to coffee, all flavors are perfectly combined in a single tiny jar.

fields.serving_size: about 1 teaspoon dry blend
what_to_add: ½–1 teaspoon per batch of muffins or quick bread
¼ teaspoon per cup of oatmeal
instructions: Put the cinnamon, ginger, nutmeg, allspice, and cloves into a small bowl.
Stir with a spoon properly. Do this until the darker spices are evenly distributed throughout the cinnamon.
Transfer the new blend to a small spice jar.
Tap the jar slightly to settle the powder. Close the lid and label the jar.
fields.storage: Store the jar tightly closed and protect it from heat and sunlight. It will keep for about a year, although the aroma will be strongest during the first several months.

title: Mexican-Style Seasoning
intro: Rice and beans can be perfectly good on their own, but I reach for this when they need a little more going on. It also works with chicken, ground beef, roasted vegetables, and skillet meals.

fields.serving_size: about 1 tablespoon dry seasoning
what_to_add: 1 tablespoon per 1 ½ cups cooked rice or beans
1 tablespoon per pound of chicken or beef
instructions: Add the chili powder, paprika, and cumin in a bowl.
Then mix these spices with the garlic powder, onion powder, oregano, black pepper, and salt.
Keep mixing properly. Also, scrape around the bottom of the bowl while you are mixing everything together.
Transfer this dry seasoning mix to a dry spice jar and close tightly.
fields.storage: Store airtight in a cool, dry pantry. For the fullest flavor, use within about 6 months.

title: Low-Sodium All-Purpose Seasoning
intro: Flavor doesn't affect much with less salt. Garlic, onion, herbs, and spices are the main ingredients in this blend, so you can season the cuisine first and know how much more salt it really needs.

fields.serving_size: about 1 tablespoon for making one portion meal
ingredients: 2 tablespoons of finely minced garlic powder
what_to_add: 1 teaspoon per pound of meat or poultry
½ teaspoon per pound of vegetables or potatoes
Add salt separately only if needed for the finished dish
instructions: Put the paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, parsley, oregano, basil, pepper, mustard, and salt into a bowl.
Whisk slowly until the mixture looks evenly colored.
Check the bottom of the bowl for any pockets of salt or mustard and mix again if needed.
Add to a clean, dry jar and seal.
fields.storage: Keep tightly sealed in a dry cabinet away from heat and sunlight. For the best flavor, use within 6 months.

title: Kid-Friendly Mild Seasoning Blend
intro: Not every person at the table desires the same level of heat. You can use the same combination for chicken, beef, potatoes, rice, and veggies since it keeps dinner well-seasoned without the chili-pepper kick.

fields.serving_size: approximately 1 tablespoon of this dry seasoning
what_to_add: 1 tablespoon per pound of ground beef, chicken, or turkey
2 teaspoons per pound of potatoes or vegetables
1 tablespoon per 2 cups cooked rice or pasta
instructions: Add the paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, and parsley in a bowl. Next, add the oregano, cumin, black pepper, and salt.
Mix everything using a spoon until the herbs and powders are properly mixed with each other.
Shift the prepared blend into an airtight jar and close properly so no air can enter inside.
fields.storage: Keep this mix in an airtight jar in a cool, dry kitchen pantry. It’s best to use it within 6 months for the best flavor.

title: Classic Pancake Mix
intro: There’s something nice about having pancake breakfast mostly decided before anyone gets hungry. This jar keeps the dry ingredients together, so when you want to cook the pancakes, add the wet ingredients and the batter is ready.

fields.serving_size: about ½ cup dry mix, makes 3 to 4 pancakes
instructions: Add and whisk the flour with the sugar, baking powder, baking soda, and salt together in a large bowl.
Run a whisk through the mixture several times, especially around the bottom of the bowl, to make sure the baking powder and baking soda are evenly distributed.
Divide the dry mix into an airtight container or jar, leaving enough room to scoop it out easily.
fields.storage: Keep the dry mix tightly sealed in the pantry for up to 3 months. Label the jar with the date you made it and the name of the blend.

title: Gluten-Free Pancake Mix
intro: This is the jar to reach for when you want pancakes without pulling three different gluten-free flours out of the pantry. The blend is mild enough for syrup, berries, or whatever you normally put on a pancake.

fields.serving_size: about ½ cup dry mix for one serving pancakes
ingredients: ¼ cup of sugar in granulated form
instructions: Put the oat flour, rice flour, tapioca flour, and all other mentioned ingredients like sugar, baking powder, baking soda, salt, and xanthan gum into a large bowl.

Whisk them all with each other for at least 30 seconds. While whisking, lift the mixture from the bottom as you go. This is especially important for the proper mixing of a small amount of xanthan gum.
Transfer the finished mix to a clean, dry, airtight container. Label and store for future use.
fields.storage: Store airtight in the pantry for up to 2 months. You can also refrigerate for up to 4 months for longer storage.

title: Waffle Mix
intro: When the breakfast has to be waffles, you know what makes it the easiest? A pre-made waffle blend. When flour and leavening are already measured and in your pantry in the right proportions, you can make breakfast quick and tasty without measuring everything.

fields.serving_size: about ½ cup dry mix for a one-person portion
instructions: Add the flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda, and salt to a large bowl.
Whisk everything thoroughly, paying attention to the bottom and sides of the bowl. This ensures that nothing is stuck at the bottom and everything is properly mixed.
Pour the mix into an airtight container and seal after labelling its name and date.
fields.storage: Keep the dry mix in an airtight container in a cool, dry pantry for up to 3 months.

title: Blueberry Muffin Mix
intro: This is the kind of jar that has a pre-made mix to help make a homemade breakfast feel much more manageable. The dry ingredients are already perfectly measured. So, when you bake, you only need the wet ingredients and blueberries.

fields.serving_size: about ¼ cup dry mix
instructions: Whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder, salt, and baking soda together.
Pour the mixture into a clean, dry 1-quart jar or airtight container.
Seal and label the container with the recipe name and date.
fields.storage: Keep the dry mix airtight in the pantry for up to 3 months. If using frozen blueberries later, keep them separately frozen until baking day.

title: Banana Bread Mix
intro: The bananas are the one part you can't put in the jar, and that's perfectly fine. When a few ripe bananas are sitting on the counter, the rest of the recipe is already measured and waiting. So, make the banana bread in no time while not worrying about the flavor at all.

fields.serving_size: about ¼ cup dry mix for one banana bread serving
instructions: Whisk the flour, sugar, baking soda, baking powder, salt, and cinnamon together.
Transfer the mixture to an airtight jar or container.
fields.storage: Keep the dry mix sealed in the pantry for up to 3 months.

title: Gluten-Free Muffin Mix
intro: When you have a pre-made gluten-free baking mix sitting nicely in your kitchen pantry, the breakfast or snack decision gets much easier. You can easily make the delicious muffins without pulling several specialty flours out of the cabinet.

fields.serving_size: about 1/3 cup dry mix
instructions: Combine all of the dry ingredients in a large bowl.
Whisk thoroughly so the xanthan gum and leavening are dispersed throughout the flours.
Transfer the mixture to an airtight container. Label and store it.
fields.storage: Store airtight in the pantry for up to 2 months, or refrigerate for up to 4 months.

title: Biscuit Mix
intro: Biscuits are much easier when the flour, baking powder, and salt are all already perfectly mixed in the same jar. When you need them, you add the cold butter and milk and go straight to the dry mixing.

fields.serving_size: about ½ cup dry mix for 2 biscuits
ingredients: 2 tablespoons of sugar in granulated form
instructions: Whisk the flour, baking powder, baking soda, salt, and sugar together.
Transfer the dry mixture to an airtight container. Label it.
fields.storage: Keep the dry mix sealed in the pantry for up to 3 months. Once butter is added, the prepared dough should be baked promptly.

title: All-Purpose Bread Mix
intro: Bread takes a little more patience than pancakes, but the measuring doesn't have to. This jar keeps the dry ingredients ready so you can spend your time on the dough instead of lining up flour, yeast, and sugar from scratch.

fields.serving_size: about ⅓ cup dry mix
instructions: Whisk the flour, instant yeast, sugar, and salt together in a large bowl.
Transfer the mixture to an airtight container and label it properly.
Seal it correctly.
fields.storage: Keep the dry mix airtight in a cool, dry pantry for up to 2 months. Keep the yeast sealed from moisture.

title: Dinner Roll Mix
intro: Dinner doesn't have to mean starting the rolls from the very first step. This jar has all the dry ingredients. So, you only have to turn them into soft rolls while dinner comes together.

fields.serving_size: about ⅓ cup dry mix
instructions: Combine the flour, yeast, sugar, and salt in a bowl.
Pour the mixture into an airtight container and label and seal.
fields.storage: Store the dry mix airtight in a cool pantry for up to 2 months. Keep moisture away from the yeast.

title: Pizza Dough Mix
intro: Friday-night pizza gets much easier when the flour and yeast are already measured. The jar won't make the pizza for you, but it removes one of the less exciting parts of starting from scratch.

fields.serving_size: about 2/3 cup dry mix
instructions: Mix the bread flour, yeast, sugar, and salt thoroughly.
Transfer the dry mixture to an airtight container.
fields.storage: Keep sealed in a cool, dry pantry for up to 2 months. Keep the yeast protected from moisture.

title: Chocolate Chip Cookie Mix
intro: You want to make a chocolate chip cookie? You don’t have whole afternoon to spend in the kitchen? This mix helps you fulfill your cookie craving by only adding wet ingredients to the prepared dry mix and then baking it.

fields.serving_size: about 2 ½ tbsp dry mix for one cookie
instructions: Whisk the flour, baking soda, and salt together.
Add the brown sugar and granulated sugar, breaking apart any packed lumps as you mix.
Transfer the dry mixture to an airtight jar or container.
Label it and seal properly.
fields.storage: Keep the dry mix sealed in the pantry for up to 3 months. Baked cookies keep at room temperature for about 4 days or can be frozen for up to 2 months.

title: Brownie Mix
intro: This is the jar to make when you want brownies without pulling out the measuring cups for every ingredient. The dry mix is ready by following this recipe. And when it’s baking day, you have to add only the wet ingredients and get straight to the good part.

fields.serving_size: With ¼ cup of this dry blend, 1 serving of brownies will be prepared in the perfect proportions.
instructions: Whisk the flour, cocoa powder, baking powder, and salt together in a small bowl.
Then, stir in the bowl, the granulated sugar and brown sugar. While stirring, break up any clumps of brown sugar, if needed.
Add and mix in the chocolate chips in this blend.
Transfer the dry blend to a 1-quart airtight jar or container.
fields.storage: Keep the dry mix sealed in the pantry for up to 3 months. Baked brownies keep at room temperature for about 4 days or frozen for up to 2 months.

title: Gluten-Free Brownie Mix
intro: Brownies can be a hassle to make because you have to gather all the different dry baking ingredients and measure them in the perfect balance. So, this mix will solve this problem. Just make sure that you are using gluten-free ingredients

fields.serving_size: use approx. 1/5 cup dry mix for a one-person portion (1 brownie)
ingredients: ¾ cup sugar in granulated form
instructions: Whisk the rice flour, tapioca flour, cocoa powder, baking powder, and salt together.
Add both sugars and stir until the brown sugar is evenly broken apart.
Fold in the chocolate chips.
Store the finished dry mix in an airtight container. Don’t forget to label it.
fields.storage: Keep airtight in the pantry for up to 2 months. Or, for a longer storage time, simply refrigerate it for up to 4 months.

title: Granola Mix
intro: To me, breakfast waiting in the pantry is very relaxing. This is exactly what this granola mix is all about. You can bake a batch whenever you have to without gathering every ingredient from scratch. It also removes the need to worry about measuring every ingredient in the correct balance.

fields.serving_size: about ½ cup dry mix for one serving of granola
ingredients: 1 cup of almonds in chopped form
½ cup of shredded coconut, unsweetened
instructions: Mix the oats, almonds, sunflower seeds, coconut, brown sugar, cinnamon, and salt in a large bowl.
Stir everything very well. This will ensure that the smaller ingredients don't just stay unmixed and sit underneath the oats.
Transfer the properly mixed dry blend to an airtight container. Label and store it.
fields.storage: Keep the dry mix airtight in your kitchen pantry for up to 2 months. Make sure the pantry is dry and cool.

title: Overnight Oats Mix
intro: This one is for mornings when breakfast needs to happen before your brain is fully online. Everything dry is portioned ahead, so the night before you just add the milk and yogurt and put the jar in the refrigerator.

fields.serving_size: about ½ cup dry mix for one-serve bowl of oats
ingredients: ½ cup of flaxseed in ground form
instructions: Add and mix the oats, chia seeds, ground flaxseed, powdered milk, brown sugar, cinnamon, and salt in a large bowl.
Stir until the chia seeds and flaxseed are distributed properly in each other. Make sure they are not lying at the bottom.
Divide the dry mixture into 8 airtight containers of equal servings (using about ½ cup per container). Or, keep the full batch in one big jar.
For one serving, combine ½ cup mix with ½ cup milk and ¼ cup Greek yogurt.
fields.storage: Keep the dry mix airtight in the pantry for up to 2 months. Once you prepare the meal by adding milk and yogurt, refrigerate it and eat within 3 days.

title: Classic Beef Chili Mix
intro: When you want to make a pot of chili without measuring six different spices, this jar will be in your nearest reach. Using this pre-mixed, perfectly seasoned blend, just add the beef, tomatoes, and beans afterward, and your dish is done without guessing measurements.

fields.serving_size: ½ tbsp per serving
ingredients: 2 teaspoons dried onion, in minced form
instructions: Add the chili powder, paprika, cumin, dried onion, garlic powder, oregano, salt, black pepper, and cayenne to a small bowl.
Mix everything using a spoon until the color looks even throughout.
Transfer the blend to an airtight jar. A small funnel makes this easier, but a spoon works just as well.
Seal the jar and label it with the name and date.
Use about 3 tablespoons of mix for each pound of ground beef when making chili. Add the mix along with your tomatoes and beans during cooking.
fields.storage: Store tightly sealed in the pantry, away from heat and direct light, for up to 6 months.

title: White Chicken Chili Mix
intro: This herbed chicken chili is milder in flavor than tomato-based chili, but it still needs enough spice to keep a pot from becoming bland. This mixture gives that base without requiring you to know which spices go with it or not.

fields.serving_size: about ¾ tablespoon dry mix for one serving meal
what_to_add: 1 lb boneless, preferably chicken breast or thighs (Skinless)
2 cans (15 oz each) white beans, in drained and rinsed form
1 can (4 oz) green chiles, cut into long slices
instructions: Add all the measured spices into a small bowl.
Stir until the cumin and chili powder are evenly mixed through the lighter-colored ingredients.
Shift the mixture into a clean, completely dry jar.
Close tightly and label the jar.
Use about 2 tablespoons of mix per pound of chicken. Combine with chicken, white beans, broth, and any other wet ingredients called for in your chili recipe.
fields.storage: Keep sealed in an airtight jar in a cool, dry pantry. Store for up to 6 months.

title: Vegetarian Black Bean Chili Mix
intro: A meatless chili still deserves a seasoning blend with some depth. This blend focuses on cumin, chili powder, oregano, and paprika, so a pot of beans and tomatoes doesn't feel like a complex, complicated spice setup.

fields.serving_size: about 1 tablespoon dry mix
ingredients: 2 teaspoons dried onion, in minced form
what_to_add: Kidney beans, washed and rinsed completely
instructions: Combine the chili powder, cumin, paprika, dried onion, garlic powder, oregano, salt, black pepper, and smoked paprika in a bowl.
Mix thoroughly, breaking apart any clumps of chili powder.
Pour the blend into an airtight jar and seal.
Label the jar.
Use about 2½ tablespoons of mix for one pot made with about 4 cups of beans and vegetables.
fields.storage: Keep the mix in an airtight container in the pantry. Store the jar for up to 6 months. Prevent the jar from steam and moisture.

title: Chicken Noodle Soup Mix
intro: Most people don't care about the seasoning when they order chicken noodle soup. This jar keeps the herbs and aromatics together, ready for the broth, chicken, and noodles.

fields.serving_size: about 1 tbsp dry mix
ingredients: 1 tablespoon celery flakes, preferably in dried form
what_to_add: 1 lb of boneless chicken breast or thigh part, in cooked and shredded form
instructions: Place all the ingredients and herbs in a bowl.
Stir well until the herbs are evenly mixed.
Pour the mixture into a dry, airtight jar.
Seal and label.
Use about ¼ cup of mix for one large pot of chicken noodle soup. Add it to broth along with the chicken, vegetables, and noodles.
fields.storage: Put the jar tightly covered in the pantry for up to 6 months. Store away from humidity, as dried herbs get soft easily when exposed to moisture.

title: Vegetable Soup Mix
intro: You don't need the vegetables to match perfectly for a good pot of vegetable soup. This jar handles the seasoning, so you can use the fresh or frozen vegetables you already have without opening several spice containers.

fields.serving_size: about 1 tbsp
instructions: Place all the ingredients and herbs in a bowl.
Stir well until the herbs are properly mixed.
Pour the mixture into a dry, airtight jar.
Seal and label.
fields.storage: Put the jar tightly covered in the pantry for up to 6 months. Store and keep it away from humidity.

title: Broccoli Cheddar Soup Mix
intro: The creamy part of broccoli cheddar soup can wait until cooking day. This jar takes care of the dry seasoning and thickening ingredients, so you aren't measuring flour and spices while trying to keep an eye on dinner.

fields.serving_size: about 2 tbsp for 1 cup of soup
ingredients: ½ teaspoon black pepper, freshly ground
what_to_add: 2 cups of chicken or vegetable broth
3 cups of fresh broccoli, in finely chopped form
1½ cups of cheddar cheese, in shredded form
instructions: Whisk the dry milk powder, flour, and cornstarch together first.
Add the dried onion, garlic powder, parsley, salt, pepper, and paprika.
Mix thoroughly until no visible clumps of flour or cornstarch are left.
Put the mixture in an airtight jar. Seal the jar.
Use ½ cup dry mix for one batch of soup. Add the mix gradually to your liquid while whisking to prevent lumps.
fields.storage: Keep sealed in an airtight jar in a cool, dry pantry. Store it for up to 3 months. Because it contains powdered dairy, keep moisture out of the container.

title: Potato Soup Mix
intro: Once the potato soup mix is in your pantry, making soup for dinner will be easy. Fresh potatoes are used for the soup, but the rest of the seasonings are ready in the right proportions already.

fields.serving_size: about 2 tbsp for a cup of soup
ingredients: ½ cup of nonfat dry milk, in powdered form
what_to_add: 4 cups of chicken or vegetable broth
4 cups of potatoes, peeled properly and cut into cubes
instructions: Put the dry milk powder and flour into a bowl and whisk together.
Add the dried onion, garlic powder, parsley, salt, pepper, and thyme.
Mix until the herbs are evenly spread throughout the powder.
Transfer to an airtight jar.
Use ½ cup of mix for one batch of potato soup. Whisk the mix into the cooking liquid before adding the potatoes so the flour disperses evenly.
fields.storage: Store airtight in the pantry for up to 3 months. Keep away from moisture and direct heat.

title: Tomato Basil Soup Mix
intro: This is a good pantry jar for the nights when a grilled cheese suddenly sounds like dinner. The dry mix brings the herbs and seasoning together; tomatoes and broth turn it into soup when you're ready.

fields.serving_size: 1 tablespoon dry mix for one serving of soup (one person)
instructions: Add the basil, onion, garlic powder, oregano, salt, pepper, and paprika to a bowl.
Mix until the spices are evenly mixed.
Transfer to an airtight jar and close securely.
Label the jar with the name and date.
Use 2 tablespoons of mix for a batch made with about 6 cups of tomato-based soup ingredients.
fields.storage: Put the mix in an airtight jar in a cool pantry. Store for up to 6 months. Make sure to keep the dried basil safe from moisture and direct sunlight.

title: Beef Stew Mix
intro: A good beef stew doesn't require a complex ingredient list, but the seasoning needs to be balanced. This jar gives you the savory base before the beef and vegetables ever hit the pot.

fields.serving_size: about 2 tablespoons dry mix
what_to_add: Beef stew meat, washed and cut into 1-inch pieces
Carrots, peeled and cut into slices
instructions: Mix white flour and all the spices in a bowl. Whisk them together.
Add the dried onion and herbs to the bowl, and keep stirring until the mixture looks evenly blended.
Add this blended dry mixture to an airtight jar.
Seal and label clearly.
Use about 3 tablespoons of mix for a stew made with 1½ to 2 pounds of beef. Stir the mix into the cooking liquid so the flour can thicken the stew evenly.
fields.storage: Store tightly sealed in the pantry for up to 6 months. Keep the jar dry and seal it carefully.

title: Gluten-Free Soup Mix Base
intro: This pre-made soup base is needed when you are looking for a gluten-free option. It uses cornstarch instead of flour, and the soup is thickened without adding wheat.

fields.serving_size: about 2 tbsp for one serving
ingredients: 2 teaspoons of garlic in powder form
what_to_add: Cooked chicken, beef, or vegetables depending on the soup type
Non-fat or fat-free milk, if needed
instructions: Mix the cornstarch and dry milk powder in a bowl.
Then, add to the bowl the dried onion, garlic powder, parsley, thyme, salt, and pepper.
Continue mixing until the herbs are evenly distributed and there are no lumps.
Pour into a clean, dry, airtight jar and label the jar. Seal it.
fields.storage: Keep sealed in an airtight container in the pantry for up to 3 months. Use certified gluten-free ingredients if the mix is being made for someone who has gluten intolerance.

title: Ranch Dressing Mix
intro: Keep this dressing mix in your pantry so you don't have to search the kitchen cabinet. This small jar acts as ranch dressing, dip, or a quick seasoning for potatoes without keeping another bottle in the refrigerator.

fields.serving_size: about 1 tablespoon dry mix
ingredients: 1 tablespoon of dill, in dried form
instructions: Add the buttermilk powder, parsley, dill, onion, garlic powder, onion powder, chives, salt, and pepper to a dry bowl.
Whisk until the herbs and seasonings are evenly distributed.
Shift to a clean, dry jar. Seal it tightly.
Use 1 tablespoon of the mix for each batch of dressing or dip above.
fields.storage: Place the jar tightly sealed in a cool, dry pantry. Store for up to 6 months. A small jar with a closed lid works way better than a loose shaker because the buttermilk powder needs to stay dry.

title: Onion Dip Mix
intro: The benefit of making onion dip at home is that the seasoning may be prepared ahead of time. After you mix this jar once, all you have to do is mix it into sour cream when the chips go faster than expected.

fields.serving_size: about 1 tablespoon dry mix
ingredients: 1 teaspoon parsley, use the dried one
½ teaspoon of sugar, in powdered form
instructions: Crush the dried onion slightly between your fingers so the pieces are evenly mixed with the other spices.
Stir it with the onion powder, garlic powder, parsley, salt, sugar, pepper, and paprika.
Transfer the final blend into an airtight jar.
Use 2 tablespoons of the mix with the sour cream and mayonnaise for one batch of dip. Refrigerate before serving so the dried onion softens.
fields.storage: Store the mix in an airtight container for up to 6 months. Protect the jar from heat and moisture. The prepared dip keeps in the refrigerator for about 3 days.

title: Buffalo Chicken Dip Mix
intro: This handy little jar is great to keep in your pantry in case game day becomes an unexpectedly large gathering. While the cream cheese, chicken, and buffalo sauce make it the familiar dip, the mix handles the spice.

fields.serving_size: about 2 tablespoons dry mix
what_to_add: Hot sauce, any brand of your choice
instructions: Whisk all dry ingredients together until the paprika and cayenne are evenly distributed.
Transfer the mix to a dry, airtight jar.
Use the entire jar for one batch of buffalo chicken dip with the ingredients listed above.
Add the dry mix into the softened cream cheese before adding the hot sauce, chicken, and cheese. Heat until hot and creamy.
fields.storage: Keep the unopened dry mix sealed in the pantry for up to 6 months. Once prepared, refrigerate leftovers for up to 3 days and reheat gently, stirring as they warm.

title: Salsa Seasoning Mix
intro: A container of this prevents a bowl of salsa from becoming a scavenger hunt for fresh ingredients. Once the tomatoes are cold, stir in the specified blend and enjoy.

fields.serving_size: about 1 tablespoon dry mix
ingredients: 1 teaspoon of cilantro, dried and crushed
instructions: Add all dry ingredients in a small bowl.
Mix thoroughly, making sure the dried onion and herbs don't clump in one place.
Place this mixed finished blend in a labeled airtight jar
fields.storage: Place the dry seasoning sealed in the pantry. Store for up to 6 months. Refrigerate the prepared salsa and use within 3–4 days.

title: Brown Gravy Mix
intro: Undoubtedly, this Brown gravy mix is one of those jars that holds its place rapidly. This mix is ready to add to mashed potatoes, meatloaf, roast beef, or any dinner where a little gravy makes the plate feel finished.

fields.serving_size: about 2 tablespoons dry mix; makes 1 cup gravy
instructions: Mix the cornstarch and flour in a bowl.
Add the bouillon powder, onion powder, garlic powder, parsley, paprika, pepper, and thyme.
Mix properly so that the color of the finished blend gets overall even throughout, then transfer to an airtight jar.
For one cup of gravy, use 3 tablespoons of the mix with 1 cup of water and 1 tablespoon of butter. For smoother gravy, combine the dry mix with cold water before heating.
fields.storage: Store the jar sealed in a dry pantry for up to 6 months. Prevent the jar from excess heat.

title: Alfredo Sauce Mix
intro: These already-measured Alfredo sauce ingredients make pasta night much easier and less dependent on what's hiding in the refrigerator. The jar gives you the perfect seasoning blend and thick sauce.

fields.serving_size: about 2 tablespoons dry mix
ingredients: ½ cup of dry milk powder
¼ cup Parmesan cheese powder, properly grated
instructions: Add the dry milk powder and cornstarch to a bowl.
Stir in the Parmesan powder, garlic powder, onion powder, parsley, salt, and pepper.
Transfer to a completely dry, airtight container.
Use ½ cup of the mix with the milk and butter to make one batch of sauce. Whisk the dry mix into cold milk before heating to help prevent lumps.
fields.storage: Because this mix contains powdered dairy and Parmesan, keep it sealed in the pantry for up to 3 months. Refrigerate the prepared sauce and use within 3 days.

title: Marinara/Pasta Sauce Mix
intro: This is for the evenings when the cabinet contains pasta, but there isn't a jar of sauce. Without an extensive list of individual herbs, the dry mix turns canned tomatoes into a seasoned sauce.

fields.serving_size: about 1 tablespoon dry mix
instructions: Combine the dried onion, parsley, basil, garlic, oregano, paprika, sugar, salt, pepper, and red pepper flakes.
Mix until the herbs are properly distributed and mixed with each other.
Store in a clean, dry jar.
Use the entire mix with the crushed tomatoes, olive oil, and water. Simmer until the sauce achieves the desired consistency.
fields.storage: Put the dry mix in an airtight jar in the pantry for up to 6 months. If mixed into tomato sauce, refrigerate for up to 4 days or freeze for up to 3 months.

title: BBQ Sauce Mix
intro: When you need a sauce but don't want to store another half-used bottle in the fridge, a dry BBQ sauce mix comes in handy. When you're ready to cook, add the wet ingredients to the already balanced brown sugar, tomato powder, and spices.

fields.serving_size: 2 tablespoons dry mix to make one portion
ingredients: 1 tablespoon smoked paprika, in proper powder form
instructions: Mix brown sugar with tomato powder.
Add the paprika, chili powder, garlic, onion, mustard, salt, pepper, and cayenne.
Mix thoroughly and transfer to an airtight jar.
Use the entire jar with the mentioned wet ingredients. Cook until smooth and slightly thickened.
fields.storage: Keep the sealed dry mix in a cool pantry for up to 4 months.

title: Teriyaki Sauce Mix
intro: Save this jar for chicken bowls, stir-fry evenings, and dinners that require a sauce that should be done in no time. This mix doesn't take up refrigerator space between uses because everything in the jar is dry.

fields.serving_size: use just 2 tablespoons of this dry mix for one serve
ingredients: ½ teaspoon black pepper, properly ground
instructions: Mix the cornstarch and brown sugar together. While mixing, break up the sugar too, if required.
Then, add the dried onion, garlic, ginger, pepper, and red pepper flakes.
Once everything is mixed with each other, add it into a dry, airtight jar and seal.
fields.storage: Store this jar in the pantry for up to 6 months. Prevent the jar from moisture so that the cornstarch and brown sugar don’t combine with each other.

title: Rice Pilaf Mix
intro: Butter, this jar, and a pot of water: dinner's rice side is basically done before the rest of the meal even starts.

fields.yield: 1 batch (about ¾ cup dry mix), makes pilaf for 3 to 4 servings
instructions: Combine the orzo, dried onion flakes, bouillon, garlic powder, rice, and turmeric in a small container.
Store in an airtight container until ready to use.
fields.storage: Store in an airtight container in the pantry for up to 6 months.

title: Beans and Rice Seasoning Mix
intro: This seasoning packet is the flavor half of a classic beans-and-rice dinner. The dried kidney beans and rice that go with it get their own bags in the pantry.

fields.yield: 1 seasoning packet (about 3 tablespoons), enough to season one batch of beans and rice (serves 4 to 6)
ingredients: ¼ teaspoon crushed red pepper flakes
instructions: Combine the bay leaf, parsley flakes, onion flakes, seasoning salt, cumin, sugar, celery seed, minced garlic, cayenne, and red pepper flakes in a small bag or jar.
Keep the seasoning packet separate from the beans and rice until ready to cook.
fields.storage: Keep the seasoning packet in a sealed bag in the pantry for up to 6 months; store the dried beans and rice separately in their own airtight containers.

title: Instant Mashed Potato Seasoning Mix
intro: One scoop of this in a bowl with boiling water turns into potato soup faster than the kettle takes to reheat.

fields.yield: 6 servings (about ½ cup dry mix each)
instructions: Combine the potato flakes, dry milk, bouillon granules, onion, parsley, white pepper, thyme, turmeric, and seasoning salt in a bowl and stir to mix.
Pour into a 1-quart jar.
fields.storage: Store in a 1-quart airtight container in the pantry for up to 6 months.

title: Sloppy Joe Seasoning Mix
intro: A big batch of this covers sloppy joe night eight times over, so ground beef, ketchup, and this jar are the only decisions left at dinner.

fields.yield: 8 servings (3 tablespoons dry mix each, one batch seasons about 8 pounds of ground beef total)
ingredients: ½ cup light brown sugar, packed
instructions: Whisk all the ingredients together in a medium bowl until well combined.
Store in an airtight container.
fields.storage: Store in an airtight container in a cool, dry place for up to 6 months.

title: Macaroni and Cheese Mix
intro: A quarter cup of this and a pot of boiling macaroni gets you homemade mac and cheese without a single foil packet.

fields.yield: 12 servings (¼ cup dry mix each)
ingredients: ½ cup nonfat dry milk powder
instructions: Whisk the cheddar cheese powder, milk powder, and dry mustard together until very well combined, about 1 minute.
Store in an airtight container.
fields.storage: Store at room temperature in an airtight container for at least 2 months.

title: Fried Rice Seasoning Mix
intro: Four teaspoons of this stirred into a hot pan of rice and soy sauce is most of what a takeout fried rice actually tastes like.

fields.yield: 6 servings (4 teaspoons dry mix each)
instructions: Combine the sugar, nutritional yeast, onion powder, salt, and garlic powder in a small jar.
Store in an airtight container until ready to use.
fields.storage: Store in an airtight container in the pantry for up to 6 months.

title: Couscous Seasoning Mix
intro: Stir this into boiling water before the couscous goes in, and it comes out seasoned instead of plain.

fields.yield: 1 batch (about 4 teaspoons dry seasoning), enough to season one 10-ounce package of couscous (6 servings)
instructions: Combine the parsley flakes, bouillon granules, minced onion, basil, black pepper, and garlic powder in a small jar.
Store in an airtight container until ready to use.
fields.storage: Store in an airtight container in the pantry for up to 6 months.

title: Cheesy Scalloped Potato Mix
intro: Half a cup of this whisked with water and poured over sliced potatoes is scalloped potatoes without the usual cheese sauce fuss.

fields.yield: 9 servings (about ½ cup dry mix each, each serving makes one casserole with dehydrated potato slices and water)
ingredients: ½ cup dried chives or parsley
instructions: Mix all the ingredients together well.
Store in a sealed container, jar, or bag in a cool, dark place.
fields.storage: This isn't a canning recipe, so the mix's shelf life follows the powdered milk's own date; keep it sealed in a cool, dark place.

title: Hearty Lentil and Rice Mix
intro: Everything for a pot of hearty soup, lentils, rice, dried mushrooms, and seasoning, is already layered in one jar; just add water.

fields.yield: 1 batch (32-ounce jar), serves 4 to 6
ingredients: 1 cup black pearl rice or wild rice
instructions: Combine all the dry ingredients in a sealed 32-ounce jar.
Consider adding a moisture-absorbing packet for long-term storage.
fields.storage: Keep sealed at room temperature, away from light, for up to 6 months.

title: Hamburger Helper-Style Beef and Mac Mix
intro: Half a cup of this with browned beef and a splash of water is most of the way to a homemade version of the boxed dinner.

fields.yield: about 7 servings (½ cup dry mix each, enough for 1 pound of ground beef per serving)
instructions: Measure all the ingredients into a resealable bag and shake well.
Transfer to a vacuum-seal bag, mason jar, or other airtight container.
fields.storage: Store in an airtight container or vacuum-sealed bag; keeps up to a year vacuum-sealed, or use within a month if not sealed airtight.

title: Herb and Butter Rice Mix
intro: A jar of this next to a pot of broth turns plain rice into a side dish worth mentioning at the table.

fields.yield: makes about 10 cups dry mix (fills 5 pint jars or 10 jelly jars); 1 pint jar (2 cups) serves 4 to 6
ingredients: 9 cups rice (long grain white, jasmine, or basmati)
1 tablespoon dried garlic or garlic powder
instructions: Combine all the ingredients in a large bowl and mix thoroughly.
Using a funnel, portion into pint jars (2 cups each) or jelly jars (1 cup each), label, and store in the pantry.
fields.storage: Best used within about 3 months; vacuum seal the jars for longer storage.

title: Garlic Parmesan Pasta Base Mix
intro: A quarter cup of this whisked with butter and milk turns into a garlicky parmesan sauce in the time it takes pasta to boil.

fields.yield: about 15 servings (¼ cup dry mix each)
ingredients: 1 cup instant nonfat dry milk powder
instructions: Combine all the ingredients in a jar, seal, and shake to combine (or mix in a zip-top bag).
Store in an airtight container; stir before each use to redistribute settled ingredients.
fields.storage: Store in an airtight container in the pantry for up to 6 months.

title: Stuffing Mix
intro: This seasoning bag turns a bag of dried bread cubes into homemade stuffing any night the mood strikes, not just on a holiday. The bread cubes get their own bag right alongside it, so both halves are ready to grab together.

fields.yield: 3 seasoning batches (about ⅓ cup each), each batch seasons stuffing for 4 servings (12 servings total)
ingredients: ½ cup plus 1 tablespoon dried celery flakes
instructions: Combine the celery flakes, minced onion, parsley flakes, bouillon granules, poultry seasoning, and rubbed sage in a small resealable bag and mix well.
Store the seasoning bag alongside a separate bag of dried bread cubes in a cool, dry place.
fields.storage: Store in a cool, dry place for up to 1 year.

title: Sheet-Pan Dinner Seasoning Mix
intro: One jar, and dinner's basically hands-off from here. Rub it on the chicken, toss the rest with whatever vegetables are in the crisper, and the oven does the work.

fields.yield: about 5½ teaspoons (one batch), enough to season 1½ pounds of chicken and about 5 cups of vegetables for one sheet-pan dinner (4 servings)
ingredients: ½ teaspoon freshly cracked black pepper
instructions: Combine the Italian seasoning, kosher salt, garlic powder, onion powder, and black pepper in a small dish or jar.
Store in an airtight container until ready to use.
fields.storage: Keep in an airtight jar in the pantry for up to 6 months.

title: Cheesy Taco Rice Skillet Seasoning Mix
intro: Taco night leftovers turn into a whole new dinner with this one. Two spices in a jar, then rice, salsa, and whatever taco meat's already in the fridge.

fields.yield: about 1½ teaspoons (one batch), enough to season one skillet of rice (6 servings)
instructions: Stir the garlic salt and cumin together in a small jar.
Store in an airtight container until ready to use.
fields.storage: Keep in the pantry indefinitely; it's shelf-stable and ready whenever taco leftovers need a second act.

title: Chicken Enchilada Bake Seasoning Mix
intro: This one spice jar does double duty. Two tablespoons stirred into tomato sauce turns into enchilada sauce, and the rest works just as well rubbed straight onto chicken before it goes into the filling.

fields.yield: 3 servings (about 2 tablespoons dry mix each), one batch, each serving makes one batch of enchilada sauce (16 ounces tomato sauce plus ½ cup water or broth)
instructions: Combine the chili powder, cumin, onion powder, garlic powder, salt, paprika, oregano, and cocoa powder in a small bowl.
Transfer to an airtight container.
fields.storage: Store in an airtight container in the pantry for up to 6 months.

title: Slow Cooker Pot Roast Seasoning Mix
intro: A tablespoon of this rubbed over a chuck roast is most of the work done before breakfast is even over. The same jar works just as well on a pork roast or stirred into beef stew.

fields.yield: 9 servings (1 tablespoon per serving, seasons 1 pound of meat)
instructions: Combine the garlic powder, onion powder, sea salt, black pepper, parsley, oregano, thyme, rosemary, and celery seed in a small bowl or mason jar.
Store in an airtight container in the pantry.
fields.storage: Store in an 8-ounce mason jar, labeled with the date, in the pantry for up to 6 months.

title: Slow Cooker Chicken and Gravy Seasoning Mix
intro: Keep this jar next to the gravy boat. A couple of spoonfuls with melted butter and broth turns into gravy in minutes, whether it's topping mashed potatoes or a plate of biscuits.

fields.yield: 24 servings (2 tablespoons dry mix each, makes about 1 cup gravy per use)
instructions: Whisk the flour, cornstarch, powdered chicken bouillon, onion powder, garlic powder, poultry seasoning, thyme, parsley, salt, and pepper together until fully combined.
Store in an airtight jar. This batch is enough for about 24 uses.
fields.storage: Keep the dry mix in an airtight jar in the pantry for up to 6 months.

title: Slow Cooker Beef Chili Seasoning Mix
intro: Dump this jar in with the beans, beef, and broth before work, and chili's ready by dinner without touching the stove again.

fields.yield: about 6 teaspoons (one batch), enough to season one full batch of chili (8 servings)
instructions: Stir the salt-free seasoning, black pepper, garlic powder, onion powder, and chili powder together in a small jar.
Store in an airtight container until ready to use.
fields.storage: Keep in the pantry for up to 6 months.

title: Chicken Pot Pie Filling Seasoning Mix
intro: A from-scratch pot pie becomes possible on a weeknight when the sauce base is already mixed.

fields.yield: about ⅓ cup sauce mix (one batch, enough for a bit more than one 9-inch pot pie)
instructions: Combine the powdered milk, cornstarch, instant chicken bouillon, dried onion flakes, and Italian seasoning in a small jar.
Store in an airtight container until ready to use.
fields.storage: Keep in an airtight jar in the pantry for up to 6 months.

title: Cajun Chicken and Rice Skillet Seasoning Mix
intro: Smoky, a little sharp from the cayenne, and just enough for a full skillet of chicken and rice. Coats the chicken before it browns, then goes back into the pan with the rice, no other seasoning needed.

fields.yield: 2 servings (about 2 tablespoons dry mix each), one batch, each serving seasons one full recipe of Cajun chicken and rice (serves 4)
instructions: Combine the smoked paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, thyme, oregano, black pepper, cayenne, and salt in a small jar.
Store in an airtight container until ready to use.
fields.storage: Keep in the pantry for up to 6 months.

title: Chili Mac Skillet Seasoning Mix
intro: One skillet, one pot to wash, and a spice blend measured out ahead of time for weeknight comfort food.

fields.yield: about 4½ tablespoons (one batch), enough for one skillet dinner (6 servings)
instructions: Stir the flour, chili powder, smoked paprika, garlic powder, and oregano together in a small jar.
Store in an airtight container until ready to use.
fields.storage: Keep in the pantry for up to 6 months.

title: Chicken and Rice Casserole Seasoning Mix
intro: The same seasoning blend flavors both the sauce and the rice here, mixed once and used twice.

fields.yield: about 9 teaspoons (one batch), enough to season both the sauce and the rice in one casserole (8 servings)
instructions: Stir the onion powder, garlic powder, salt, black pepper, and parsley together in a small jar.
Store in an airtight container until ready to use.
fields.storage: Keep in the pantry for up to 6 months.

title: Shepherd's Pie Seasoning Mix
intro: A single-use jar: mix it up the morning of, then stir it into ground beef when shepherd's pie is on the dinner plan.

fields.yield: 1 batch (about 4¼ tablespoons dry mix), a single use that seasons 1 pound of ground beef for one shepherd's pie
instructions: Combine the cornstarch, sugar, bouillon mix, onion powder, salt, pepper, garlic powder, and cayenne in a small bowl.
Store in an airtight container until ready to use.
fields.storage: Keep in the pantry for up to 6 months.

title: Jambalaya Seasoning Mix
intro: Paprika-forward with a little heat from the cayenne, this jar turns a pot of rice, sausage, and shrimp into jambalaya without pulling five spices off the rack.

fields.yield: 1 batch (about 11½ teaspoons dry mix), enough for one pot of jambalaya
instructions: Combine the paprika, onion powder, garlic powder, oregano, black pepper, cayenne, and salt in a small bowl and mix well.
Store in an airtight container until ready to use.
fields.storage: Keep in the pantry for up to 6 months.

title: One-Pot Chicken and Rice Seasoning Mix
intro: Broth flavor, herbs, and a little cornstarch to thicken things up: this jar gets measured out ahead of time, so dinner starts before the chicken even hits the pan.

fields.yield: 1 batch (about 4¾ tablespoons dry mix), seasons 1 pound of chicken and 1 cup of rice for one pot (about 4 servings, estimated)
ingredients: 1 tablespoon chicken bouillon powder or granulated bouillon
instructions: Measure the chicken bouillon powder, onion powder, garlic powder, cornstarch, parsley, thyme, paprika, salt, black pepper, and celery salt into a small jar or airtight pouch.
Shake vigorously until uniform, then store in the pantry.
fields.storage: Keep in the pantry for up to 6 months.

title: Dry Onion Soup Mix
intro: This one lives in the back of my spice cabinet year-round. A spoonful goes into pot roast, a full jar turns into soup on its own, and I never have to remember which aisle sells the packet.
