fields.yield: 1 batch (4 servings), equivalent to one 1-ounce envelope of store-bought onion soup mix
instructions: Stir the onion flakes, bouillon granules, onion powder, parsley flakes, celery seed, paprika, and black pepper together in a small bowl until evenly blended.
Pour into a jar with a tight lid.
fields.storage: Keep the jar sealed in a cool, dry spot in your pantry. It'll hold its flavor for about 6 months.

title: Slow Cooker Pulled Pork Seasoning Mix
intro: This jar sits in the pantry until pulled pork night, then it does all the flavor work — no last-minute trip for a spice you only need once.

fields.servings_combined: Makes 11 tablespoons of dry rub. 1 tablespoon seasons 1 pound of pork.
ingredients: ¼ cup coarse ground black pepper
instructions: Stir the black pepper, salt, smoked paprika, garlic powder, and onion powder together in a small bowl or jar until evenly combined.
Transfer to an airtight jar or container.
fields.storage: Keep in an airtight jar in the pantry for up to 6 months.

title: Steak Seasoning Rub
intro: Keep this one next to the salt and pepper. No last-minute run for a bottle of steak seasoning, and no guessing at the ratio next time either.

fields.yield: 6 servings (about 2½ tablespoons rub each)
instructions: Combine the kosher salt, smoked paprika, onion powder, garlic powder, oregano, black pepper, brown sugar, and cumin in a container with a tight-fitting lid.
Seal and shake until the color is even throughout, with no streaks of any one spice.
fields.storage: Store in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. Give it a sniff before using after long storage; if it's gone quiet on smell, it's time for a fresh batch. Good for about 6 months.

title: Ranch Seasoning Blend
intro: Whenever a recipe calls for a ranch packet, or the kids want something to dip their veggies in, this jar's already sitting there. No more finding out the box expired the one week you actually needed it.

fields.yield: 12 servings (about 1 teaspoon dry blend each)
instructions: Stir the parsley, seasoned salt, pepper, garlic powder, onion powder, and thyme together in a small bowl until fully combined.
Transfer to a small jar.
fields.storage: Keep the dry blend in an airtight jar in the pantry for up to 6 months.

title: Herbes de Provence
intro: Chicken thighs, pork chops, roasted vegetables, even a simple pan of rice: anything that needs a little more going on than salt and pepper gets a pinch of this. It's a big batch too, so once it's mixed you're set for months of dinners.

fields.yield: 48 servings (about 1 teaspoon each)
ingredients: 1 teaspoon bay powder (bay leaves ground to a fine powder)
instructions: Grind the rosemary and fennel seed together in a spice grinder until fine, then transfer to a mixing bowl.
Add the savory, thyme, basil, marjoram, lavender, parsley, oregano, tarragon, and bay powder and stir well until evenly blended.
Transfer to an airtight container.
fields.storage: Store in an airtight container between uses, out of direct light. Keeps well for about a year.

title: Chicken and Dumpling Soup Base
intro: On a cold night when the kids want something warm and filling, this base is already halfway to a full pot of soup.

fields.yield: 8 servings (one batch = 8 jars, each seasoning one pot)
ingredients: ¼ teaspoon celery seed or celery powder
instructions: Add the flour, powdered milk, cornstarch, chicken bouillon powder, onion powder, garlic powder, parsley, thyme, black pepper, salt, and celery seed to a large mixing bowl.
Whisk thoroughly until completely uniform, with no streaks of any one ingredient.
Transfer to a pint-size mason jar or airtight container. Tap gently on the counter to help it settle, then seal and label with the name and date.
fields.storage: Keep in a cool, dry pantry for up to 6 months.

title: Corn Chowder Mix
intro: For the nights soup sounds right but a grocery run doesn't, this base is most of the work already done.

fields.yield: about 4 cups dry mix (8 batches of ½ cup, each seasoning one pot of chowder)
instructions: Whisk the dry milk powder, cornstarch, dried minced onions, onion powder, basil, thyme, parsley, black pepper, and potato flakes together in a large bowl until evenly blended.
Transfer to an airtight jar or container and label it.
fields.storage: Keep the dry mix in an airtight container in the pantry for up to 6 months.

title: Lentil Soup Mix
intro: Just add water and a can of coconut milk: this jar carries the lentils and the spice work, so soup night doesn't need a grocery run first.

fields.yield: 1 batch (1 pint jar), makes about 6½ cups finished soup (4 to 6 servings)
ingredients: 1 tablespoon vegetable bouillon powder (or 3 bouillon cubes)
instructions: Layer half the lentils in a pint jar, add the dried onion, bouillon, curry powder, cumin, paprika, and garlic powder, then top with the remaining lentils.
Seal and store in the pantry until ready to use.
fields.storage: Store the sealed jar in the pantry for up to 6 months.

title: Sausage Gravy Mix
intro: Biscuits and gravy doesn't have to wait for a Sunday. A pound of breakfast sausage and this jar gets you there on a Tuesday just as easily.

fields.yield: 8 servings (about 3 tablespoons dry mix each; pairs with 1 pound breakfast sausage and 1 cup water or milk per use)
instructions: Whisk the flour, dry milk powder, cornstarch, black pepper, salt, onion powder, and poultry seasoning together until well combined.
Store in an airtight jar. This batch is enough for about 8 uses.
fields.storage: Keep the dry mix in an airtight jar in the pantry for up to 6 months.

title: Italian Dressing Mix
intro: Mixed up once, this sits ready in the cabinet, so a bottle of dressing is never the reason a salad doesn't happen at dinner.

fields.yield: 16 servings (about 1 teaspoon dry mix each; 2 tablespoons makes one batch of dressing)
instructions: Mix the oregano, salt, parsley, garlic salt, onion powder, sugar, pepper, basil, thyme, and celery salt together in a bowl until evenly combined.
Store in a tightly sealed container until ready to use.
fields.storage: Keep the dry mix in a tightly sealed container in the pantry for up to 6 months.

title: Queso Dip Mix
intro: This is the mix that shows up at game nights and ordinary Tuesday movie nights alike: spices ready ahead of time, cheese and milk whenever the craving hits.

fields.yield: 6 servings, dry mix only (pairs with 1 cup milk and 8 ounces shredded cheese to make one batch of dip)
ingredients: ¼ teaspoon cayenne pepper (optional, for heat)
instructions: Measure the cornstarch, chili powder, garlic powder, onion powder, cumin, smoked paprika, salt, and cayenne (if using) into a small container or 8-ounce mason jar.
Seal tight and store in the pantry.
fields.storage: Keep the dry mix in an airtight jar in the pantry for up to 6 months.

title: Gluten-Free All-Purpose Bread Mix
intro: Skip the special trip for a boxed gluten-free bread mix: this jar already has the flour blend balanced, so bread day starts with butter, milk, and eggs instead of a recipe card.

fields.yield: 1 batch (about 3⅓ cups dry mix), makes one 1½-pound loaf when butter, milk, eggs, and yeast are added
instructions: Whisk the flour blend, xanthan gum, salt, baking soda, and sugar together until evenly combined.
Store in an airtight container until ready to use.
fields.storage: Store in an airtight container in the pantry for up to 6 months.

title: Gluten-Free Pizza Dough Mix
intro: The same gluten-free flour blend that goes into a loaf of sandwich bread stretches into a pizza crust too, just with yeast, eggs, warm water, and olive oil worked in instead of butter and milk.

fields.yield: 1 batch (about 3⅓ cups dry mix), makes one pizza crust when yeast, eggs, warm water, and olive oil are added
instructions: Whisk the flour blend, xanthan gum, salt, baking soda, and sugar together until evenly combined.
Store in an airtight container until ready to use.
fields.storage: Store in an airtight container in the pantry for up to 6 months.

fields.yield: 1 batch (about 1 cup dry mix), enough to season 2½ cups macaroni with plant milk (about 5 servings)
instructions: Combine the nutritional yeast, flour, salt, sugar, garlic powder, onion powder, smoked paprika, black pepper, and turmeric in a jar.
Seal and store in a cool, dark place until ready to use.
fields.storage: Store in a cool, dark place in a sealed jar for up to 6 months.

title: Dairy-Free Ranch Dressing Mix
intro: The classic ranch flavor, no buttermilk powder involved, so it works over salad, roasted vegetables, or a bowl of chicken without anyone checking the label for dairy.

fields.yield: 6 tablespoons (about 24 servings at ¼ teaspoon each)
instructions: Crush the dried parsley between your fingers or in a spice grinder to break it down slightly.
Combine the parsley, garlic powder, onion powder, black pepper, and salt in a jar, seal, and shake well.
fields.storage: Store in a covered jar in the pantry; shake before each use, since the parsley settles out from the rest of the blend.

title: Gluten-Free Gravy Mix
intro: One tablespoon of this in place of a store packet, and a gluten-containing gravy mix is off the ingredient list without giving up gravy at dinner.

fields.yield: about 2 cups dry mix (about 32 servings, 1 tablespoon dry mix each)
ingredients: 6 tablespoons crushed low-sodium beef bouillon cubes
instructions: Combine the cornstarch, crushed bouillon, onion powder, garlic powder, and pepper in a jar with a tight lid.
Seal and shake thoroughly until evenly blended.
fields.storage: Store in an airtight jar in the pantry for up to 6 months.

title: Dairy-Free Chocolate Chip Cookie Mix
intro: Layered in a jar, this one just needs oil and vanilla stirred in to turn into a batch of cookies, dairy-free chocolate chips and all.

fields.yield: 1 batch (about 4 cups dry mix), makes about 24 cookies when oil and vanilla are added
ingredients: ½ cup dairy-free dark chocolate chips
instructions: Combine the flour, baking powder, salt, and cinnamon in a jar or container.
Layer the dried cranberries, sugar, and dairy-free chocolate chips on top, then seal.
fields.storage: Store in an airtight container in the pantry for up to 3 months.

title: Gluten-Free Taco Seasoning Kit
intro: Same taco night, minus the wheat starch some packet blends sneak in. A spoonful of this and a splash of water gets the same result.

fields.yield: 3 seasoning packets (about 6 teaspoons each), each packet seasons about 1 pound of meat
instructions: Whisk all the spices together in a small bowl until evenly blended.
Divide into three portions and store each in a small jar or airtight container.
fields.storage: Label and store in a glass jar or airtight container in the pantry for up to 6 months.

title: Dairy-Free Biscuit Mix
intro: Shortening stands in for butter here, so this one is dairy-free straight out of the jar. Add a milk of your choice at baking time and it turns into biscuits, dumplings, or shortcakes without a special trip to the store.

fields.yield: 1 batch (about 6 cups dry mix); each 3-cup portion makes about 24 biscuits when combined with milk
instructions: Combine the flour, shortening, baking powder, salt, and baking soda in a food processor and pulse until evenly blended, about 5 pulses.
Store in the refrigerator or freezer until ready to use.
fields.storage: Store in the refrigerator or freezer, not the pantry, for up to 3 months; the cut-in shortening can turn rancid at room temperature.
